stories.title: Amar Dedic set to escape Newcastle sanction over carrying bow and arrow
summary: Right-back sparked armed police response over incidentExpected to start Newcastle’s trip to Fulham on SaturdayNewcastle’s Amar Dedic is unlikely to face a club sanction after being spotted holding a bow and arrow in the Northumberland countryside and sparking a major police pursuit involving an armed response unit.Dedic is expected to start Newcastle’s match at Fulham on Saturday after an incident that at one point saw six patrol cars pursue the ­Bosnia right‑back back to his home on the Darras Hall estate, just ­outside Ponteland.

stories.title: ‘Clicky Ponting’ cheating scandal cricketer banned and club relegated
summary: Brian Devine, 38, banned from all cricket for two yearsSaltburn 2nd XI relegated and club fined by leagueThe club cricketer dubbed “Clicky Ponting” in response to accusations of cheating during the English summer has been handed a two-year ban from the sport.

His team, Saltburn CC’s 2nd XI, have also been relegated.Brian Devine earned online notoriety back in July after footage from Division Two of the North Yorkshire and South Durham Cricket League went viral.

The ban covers “playing, coaching, umpiring, scoring and managing junior teams”.After an appeal against their sanction, Saltburn CC have been fined £300 and their 2nd XI has been relegated to Division Three of the NYSDCL.

stories.title: Jobe Bellingham joins brother Jude in England squad as King and White included
summary: Spence back but no Mainoo, Palmer or O’ReillyMadueke also overlooked but Gibbs-White inJobe Bellingham has been given a first England call-up by Thomas Tuchel, joining his brother Jude in the squad.

The head coach has also called up Josh King and Ben White for Nations League matches against Croatia and Spain.Kobbie Mainoo, Cole Palmer, Noni Madueke and Nico O’Reilly are not in the squad – Tuchel said O’Reilly had to take care of an injury – but Djed Spence has returned.
Dean Henderson and Jordan Henderson remain on the outside but Trent Alexander-Arnold has retained his place.

stories.title: Hockey’s streaming spree means there’s one fewer thing holding Canada together
summary: But it’s becoming increasingly difficult – and expensive – to watch games on televisionThe Oilers lost to the Detroit Red Wings on 26 October, but Edmonton captain Connor McDavid got an assist anyway.
Just 16 games into the year, McDavid has 31 assists.

The NHL also expanded its broadcast deal with Amazon, so when, two nights after the game against Detroit, the Oilers played their provincial rival, the Calgary Flames, only Amazon Prime subscribers could watch (true to form, McDavid got two assists in that one).

summary: The Norwegian, 35, has set up a training camp in Spain to prepare for the Budapest Total Chess pilotNovember will be an important month for global chess, with the Total World Championship pilot, combining fast classical, rapid and blitz segments due in Budapest from 10-20 November.

This will be followed by the Gukesh Dommaraju v Javokhir Sindarov Fide World Championship match in Geneva between 24 November and 12 December, featuring 14 games of classical chess ­followed, if needed, by rapid and blitz tie-breaks.The traditional London Classic at the Novotel West in Hammersmith will also start on 24 November and will continue until 7 December.

stories.title: Win at Everton would put Coventry on right side of history in survival fight
summary: None of the 21 sides who had 12 points after 10 matches, over the past decade, were relegated from the Premier LeagueIf Coventry win at Everton on Friday night they will take an enormous stride towards maintaining their Premier League status.
That might seem a huge statement with 28 games remaining, but victory would put Frank Lampard’s side on the right side of recent history.
For now, they stand on a precipice.Coventry have taken nine points from nine league matches.
